new.exam_name: APPSC Group 1 (Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission Group-I Services Examination)
new.aliases: APPSC Group I; AP Group 1; Andhra Pradesh Group 1 Services; APPSC Deputy Collector exam
new.mode: Pen & Paper Based (objective prelims; descriptive mains)
new.last_date: As per notification (2026 cycle: 9 November 2026 after extension)
new.test_date: As per notification (2026 cycle prelims: 24 January 2027)
new.marking: +1/-0.33 (1/3 mark deducted per wrong answer, per Adda247)
new.eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university (some posts need a specific degree, e.g. DSP Communications needs B.E./B.Tech in ECE or related). Age 18 to 42 years, raised to 44 for non-uniformed posts by G.O.Ms.No.187 (valid to 30 Sep 2027); DSP posts have lower upper limits. Relaxations for SC/ST/BC (5 years) and PwBD (10 years). Candidates from any state may apply, but non-local candidates compete only in open (unreserved) seats; local status needs AP certificates.
new.application_fee: Rs. 370/- (Rs. 250/- processing + Rs. 120/- exam fee); SC/ST/BC/PwBD/ex-servicemen, white ration card holders and unemployed youth of AP pay only Rs. 250/-
new.paper_pattern: Prelims (screening only) has two objective papers of 120 questions, 120 marks and 120 minutes each: Paper I General Studies (history and culture, polity, economy, geography) and Paper II General Aptitude (mental ability, science and technology, current events). Available in English and Telugu. Prelims marks do not count for final merit; about 50 candidates per post go to Mains.
new.selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (5 descriptive papers of 150 marks + qualifying Telugu and English papers) → Interview (75 marks) → Document verification
new.remarks: Final merit is out of 825 (750 Mains + 75 interview). Posts and vacancies change every notification; confirm on psc.ap.gov.in.

applicants.note: Prelims held 17 March 2024 under Notification 12/2023 (81 posts); Careers360 reports 1,48,881 registered and 91,463 appeared (72.55%). The 72.55% matches 91,463 out of about 1.26 lakh, not 1.49 lakh, so the percentage base is unclear. No later prelims has been held yet.

vacancies.note: Advt. No. 07/2026 (notified 15 Sep 2026), 166 posts across 13 post codes including carry-forward. An earlier Hans India report (15 Sep 2026) listed 163 posts; the detailed notification is reported as 166.

new.notes: The official site psc.ap.gov.in / portal-psc.ap.gov.in could not be opened (certificate error), so notification details come from Testbook and Adda247 summaries of Advt. 07/2026. Sources conflict on fee wording (Rs. 250 vs Rs. 270 processing) and on vacancies (163 vs 166). Applicant figures are from the 2023 notification cycle (prelims March 2024; 4,496 qualified for Mains). Latest completed cycle: Notification 12/2023 (Mains May 2025). 2026 cycle prelims is scheduled for 24 Jan 2027.

new.exam_name: APPSC CCE (Arunachal Pradesh Public Service Combined Competitive Examination)
new.aliases: APPSCCE; Arunachal PSC CCE; Arunachal Pradesh Civil Service exam; APCS exam
new.test_date: As per notification (2026 cycle prelims: 6 December 2026; 2024 cycle: 15 December 2024)
new.eligibility: Graduate degree from a recognised university (final-year students may apply provisionally). Open only to citizens who are permanent residents of Arunachal Pradesh (PRC) and hold an Arunachal Pradesh Scheduled Tribe (APST) certificate, and who can speak an indigenous tribal language of the state (2026 rule). Age 21 to 35 years on the last date of application (20 Oct 2026); relaxation of 5 years for APST, more for PwBD and disabled defence personnel.
new.paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers of 200 marks and 2 hours each, set in English: Paper I General Studies (decides who goes to Mains) and Paper II Aptitude Test (CSAT), which is qualifying with 33% needed. About 12 times the number of vacancies are admitted to Mains. Prelims marks do not count for final merit.
new.selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (8 descriptive papers incl. qualifying English) → Interview (275 marks) → Document verification & medical (physical tests for police posts)
new.remarks: Only APST permanent residents of Arunachal Pradesh are eligible from the 2026 cycle. The exam is not held every year (the 2024 cycle came after a gap of about four years).

applicants.note: APPSCCE (Prelims) 2024, held 15 Dec 2024; NENOW reports 17,009 candidates appeared (afternoon CSAT session); 1,658 qualified for Mains (official result notice 22 Dec 2024 lists roll numbers only). Registered count not found on an opened page.

vacancies.note: Advertisement No. 5/2026 dated 7 Sep 2026: 135 posts in 13 services (APCS 60, APPS 10, Assistant Section Officer 38, others). The 2024 cycle had 140 vacancies per news reports.

new.notes: Short name kept as 'APPSC CCE' to separate it from Andhra's 'APPSC Group 1'. Eligibility, fee, pattern and vacancies are from the official 2026 advertisement (scanned PDF, read page by page). Mains merit papers: Essay, GS I-IV, Optional I-II (1,750 marks total); English (300 marks) is qualifying at 33%. Applicant figure is for the 2024 cycle; the 2024 Mains was still being processed in 2026 per APPSC notices. No 2025 cycle was held.

new.exam_name: APSC CCE (Assam Public Service Commission Combined Competitive Examination)
new.aliases: APSC CCE; Assam PSC; Assam Civil Service exam; ACS exam; APSC prelims
new.test_date: As per notification (CCE 2025 prelims: 5 July 2026; CCE 2024 prelims: 8 June 2025)
new.eligibility: Degree from a recognised university. Indian citizen, original inhabitant of Assam, registered in a District Employment Office of Assam, and able to speak Assamese or another official/associate official language or a tribal language of the state. Age 21 to 38 years on 1 Jan 2025 (CCE 2025); relaxed by 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC/MOBC and 10 years for PwBD.
new.application_fee: Rs. 297.20/- (General: Rs. 250/- + Rs. 47.20/- processing); OBC/MOBC Rs. 197.20/-; SC/ST, BPL, PwBD and all women pay only the Rs. 47.20/- processing fee
new.paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers of 200 marks and 2 hours each: General Studies I (30-35% of questions on Assam) and General Studies II, which is qualifying (33% needed). Prelims is screening only; marks do not count for final merit. Papers were set in Assamese and English in 2026.
new.selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (6 descriptive papers, 1,500 marks: Essay, GS I-IV, Assam paper) → Interview (180 marks) → Document verification
new.remarks: Mains is held only in Guwahati. Vacancies vary sharply between cycles (262 in CCE 2024, 78 in CCE 2025); confirm on apsc.nic.in.

applicants.note: CCE (Preliminary) 2025, held 5 July 2026 at 74 venues: Assam Tribune reports 41,695 applicants (23,218 male, 18,473 female, 4 transgender) for 78 posts. Appeared count not given in the article.

vacancies.note: Advt. No. 01/2026 dated 10 Apr 2026 for CCE 2025: 78 posts across 11 services (Assam Civil Service Jr. Grade 45). Previous cycle (CCE 2024, Advt. 12/2025) had 262 posts.

new.notes: Naming: APSC labels the exam by year of vacancies, so 'CCE 2025' was advertised and held in 2026. Eligibility, fee, negative marking and vacancies are from the official scanned advertisements. Mains/interview marks from apsc.nic.in/cce.html. Aggregators report 958 qualified for CCE 2025 Mains (not verified on an official page). For CCE 2024, Sentinel reports 3,538 qualified for Mains.

new.exam_name: BPSC CCE (Bihar Public Service Commission Combined Competitive Examination)
new.aliases: BPSC; BPSC 71st CCE; Bihar PCS; BPSC Integrated CCE; Bihar civil services exam
new.eligibility: Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university. Minimum age 21 years (varies by post); maximum 37 years for general men, 40 for general women and BC/EBC, 42 for SC/ST (71st CCE, age counted on 1 Aug 2025 per aggregators). Reservation and fee concessions are only for Bihar residents; other-state candidates compete as general category.
new.application_fee: Rs. 600/- (Rs. 150/- for SC/ST of Bihar, women who are Bihar residents, and PwD); plus Rs. 200/- biometric fee
new.paper_pattern: Prelims is one objective General Studies paper of 150 questions, 150 marks, 2 hours. It is screening only; about 10 times the vacancies are called to Mains.
new.selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (General Hindi qualifying + General Studies and essay papers, descriptive) → Interview (120 marks) → Document verification
new.remarks: One of the largest state PSC exams by applicants. Posts and vacancies change every notification and are often revised upward after the advert; confirm on bpsc.bihar.gov.in.

applicants.note: 71st CCE prelims, 13 Sep 2025. Appeared = 3,16,905 from the scanned BPSC result notice (copy hosted on Testbook's CDN; the BPSC site list did not load); 13,368 qualified for Mains. Registered ~4.71 lakh is from an IANS report citing official data (freepressjournal.in), rounded; Testbook gives 4,71,012 but its appeared figure (3,16,762) does not match the notice.

vacancies.note: BPSC exam calendar lists 1,298 vacancies for the Integrated 71st CCE. The advert (May 2025) had 1,250, raised to 1,264 in June 2025, and later to 1,298. The 72nd CCE is listed with 1,189 vacancies and prelims on 17 Jan 2027.

new.notes: The official 71st advertisement PDF could not be opened (BPSC advertisement list loads dynamically), so eligibility and fee are from news/aggregators. Negative marking is left blank: sources conflict (Careers360: 1/3 per wrong answer; PW: 0.25; BPSC overview page says none). Mains structure also conflicts: BPSC overview page lists GS I, GS II and a 300-mark optional; aggregators list GS I, GS II and Essay at 300 each with a qualifying 100-mark optional. 71st Mains (25-29 Apr 2026): 11,125 appeared; result 6 Nov 2026 called 3,185 to interview (Careers360 citing BPSC).

new.exam_name: CGPSC SSE (Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission State Service Examination)
new.aliases: CGPSC; CG PSC State Service Exam; Rajya Seva Pariksha; CG PCS; CGPSC Deputy Collector exam
new.marking: +2/-0.67 (1/3 of marks deducted per wrong answer)
new.eligibility: Degree from a recognised university (final-year students may sit prelims). Age 21 to 30 years on 1 Jan 2025 for most posts; Chhattisgarh domicile candidates may be up to 35 (+5 years for educated unemployed of CG); DSP 21 to 28. SC/ST/OBC of CG get 5 more years, CG women 10 more, with a combined cap of 45. Reservation only for CG domicile; others compete as unreserved.
new.application_fee: Rs. 400/- (Rs. 300/- for Chhattisgarh-domicile SC/ST/OBC non-creamy layer and PwD), plus portal fee and GST; CG-domicile candidates who appear in the written exam/interview can claim an exam fee refund
new.paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers of 100 questions, 200 marks and 2 hours each: Paper I General Studies (decides Mains shortlist, about 15 times vacancies) and Paper II Aptitude Test (qualifying). Minimum 33% (23% reserved) in each paper.
new.selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (7 descriptive papers of 200 marks: Language, Essay, GS I-V; 1,400 marks) → Interview (100 marks) → Document verification
new.remarks: Mains Language paper and Essay include Chhattisgarh-specific content. Posts and vacancies change every notification; confirm on psc.cg.gov.in.

vacancies.note: SSE 2025, Advt. 06/2025 dated 26 Nov 2025: 238 posts in the original advert, 239 after the 3 Dec 2025 corrigendum, 265 after the 12 Dec 2025 corrigendum added cooperative department posts (20 post types).

new.notes: Eligibility, fee, pattern and vacancies from the official SSE-2025 advertisement and corrigendum. SSE 2025 prelims held 22 Feb 2026; 3,921 shortlisted for Mains (Careers360, 26 Mar 2026). No applied/appeared count was found on any opened page, so applicants is null. Fee wording summarised from Hindi para 18 of the advert.

new.exam_name: Goa PSC JSO (Goa Public Service Commission Junior Scale Officer, Goa Civil Service Recruitment)
new.aliases: Goa PSC; GPSC Goa; Goa Civil Service; Junior Scale Officer Goa; GCS exam
new.mode: Computer Based (pre-screening and screening CBRT); written exam and interview after that
new.eligibility: Degree from a recognised university. Knowledge of Konkani is essential (Marathi desirable). Age not more than 40 years on the last date of application; government may relax for certain categories, but never beyond 50.
new.paper_pattern: Pre-screening test: 60 MCQs, 60 marks, 75 minutes (50 marks reasoning and numerical aptitude, 10 marks English comprehension), no negative marking; pass mark 65% for General/EWS, 60% OBC/PwD, 55% SC/ST, with a repeat test for borderline scores. Then a screening CBRT of 75 marks in 90 minutes (polity, history, geography, environment, current affairs, English, reasoning).
new.selection_process: Pre-screening test (CBRT) → Screening test (CBRT, 75 marks) → Competitive written exam (250 marks) → Oral interview (40 marks) → Final merit on written + interview
new.remarks: Goa does not hold a regular yearly combined state civil services exam; GPSC advertises Junior Scale Officer (Goa Civil Service) posts on its own from time to time. Watch gpsc.goa.gov.in for the next advertisement.

vacancies.note: Advertisement No. 09 of 2025 (5 Sep 2025): 38 Junior Scale Officer posts (16 UR, 11 OBC, 6 ST, 5 EWS; 1 CFF and 3 PwD within these).

new.notes: Goa has no regular combined competitive exam; this record covers the GPSC Junior Scale Officer (Goa Civil Service) recruitment, the closest equivalent. Short name 'Goa PSC JSO' avoids clash with Gujarat's GPSC. Application fee is not given in the advertisement text (it refers to online/e-challan payment only). Applicant numbers were not found. Pre-screening was held 13-14 June 2026; later stages' results were not checked.

new.test_date: As per notification (2026 cycle prelims: 7 June 2026; mains October 2026)
new.eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university (final-year students may sit prelims). Age 20 to 35 years; upper age relaxed for SC/ST/SEBC/EWS (to 40 for men, 45 for women), unreserved women (40), PwBD (45) and ex-servicemen.
new.application_fee: Rs. 100/- plus charges (no fee for SC, ST, SEBC, EWS, PwBD and ex-servicemen)
new.paper_pattern: Prelims is one objective General Studies paper of 200 marks and 3 hours. It is qualifying only; marks do not count for final merit.
new.selection_process: Prelims (objective, qualifying) → Mains (Gujarati and English qualifying papers + 5 essay/GS papers, 1,250 marks) → Personality test (150 marks) → Document verification
new.remarks: Mains has compulsory Gujarati and English language papers. Posts and vacancies change every notification; confirm on gpsc.gujarat.gov.in / gpsc-ojas.gujarat.gov.in.

new.exam_name: HPSC HCS (Haryana Public Service Commission Haryana Civil Services Executive Branch and Other Allied Services Examination)
new.aliases: HCS; HCS Ex Br; Haryana Civil Services exam; HPSC HCS; Haryana PCS
new.test_date: As per notification (latest prelims: 26 April 2026; Mains 27-29 June 2026)
new.marking: +1/-0.25 (one-fourth mark deducted per wrong answer; five options incl. 'not attempted')
new.eligibility: Bachelor of Arts, Science or Commerce degree or equivalent from a recognised university. Age 18 to 42 years on 1 Jan 2026 (DSP: 18 to 27). Upper age relaxed 5 years for SC and BC of Haryana, and for PwBD, widows and some other groups; reserved-category benefits only for Haryana residents.
new.application_fee: Rs. 1000/- (Rs. 250/- for DSC, OSC, BC-A, BC-B, ESM, EWS and women of Haryana; no fee for PwBD of Haryana)
new.paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers of 100 marks and 2 hours each, bilingual (English and Hindi): Paper I General Studies and Paper II Civil Services Aptitude Test (qualifying, 33% needed). Mains shortlist (about 12 times vacancies) is based on Paper I alone; prelims marks do not count for final merit.
new.selection_process: Prelims (objective, screening) → Mains (6 descriptive papers of 100 marks: English, Hindi, GS I-IV) → Personality test / viva-voce (75 marks) → Final merit on 675 marks
new.remarks: Need at least 45% aggregate and 33% in each of English and Hindi in Mains to be called for interview. Posts change every notification; confirm on hpsc.gov.in.

vacancies.note: Advt. No. 22/2026 (HCS & Allied Services 2025), published 30 Jan 2026: 102 posts (HCS Ex. Br. 24, DSP 8, ETO 27, AETO 22, others). A corrigendum dated 5 Feb 2026 exists and was not checked.

new.notes: All details from the official scanned advertisement (read page by page). HPSC 'What's New' lists the final result/service allocation for this cycle on 17 Oct 2026, so the 2025-exam cycle is complete. No applied/appeared figure was found (web search quota ran out before news could be checked), so applicants is null. Previous adverts: 58/2023 (HCS 2023), 11/2023 (HCS 2022).

new.aliases: HPAS; HP PCS; HPPSC CCE; Himachal Administrative Service exam; HPAS-CCE
new.test_date: As per notification (2026 cycle prelims: 13 December 2026, two sessions)
new.eligibility: Bachelor's degree or equivalent from a recognised university. Age 21 to 35 years as on 1 Jan 2026 (relaxations as per HP government rules).
new.paper_pattern: Prelims has two objective papers in two sessions on the same day (10 am-12 noon and 2-4 pm). Detailed marks and negative marking could not be confirmed from an official page.
new.remarks: Few posts are offered each year. Confirm all details in the official notification on hppsc.hp.gov.in.

new.exam_name: JKPSC CCE (Jammu and Kashmir Public Service Commission Combined Competitive Examination)
new.aliases: JKPSC; JKAS exam; J&K Combined Competitive Exam; JKPSC CCE; Jammu Kashmir Administrative Service exam
new.forms_out: As per notification (CCE 2025 Mains forms: February-March 2026)
new.eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university and J&K domicile. Age limit listed by Adda247 as '32 to 35 years as on 01.01.2025' (upper limit varies by category; unverified).
new.application_fee: Rs. 1200/- (Rs. 700/- for reserved categories; no fee for PHC candidates) for the Mains, per Adda247

new.exam_name: JPSC CCE (Jharkhand Public Service Commission Combined Civil Services Examination)
new.aliases: JPSC; Jharkhand PCS; JPSC Civil Services; Jharkhand Sanyukt Asainik Seva Pratiyogita Pariksha; JCCE
new.test_date: As per notification (CCE 2025 prelims: 19 April 2026; Mains 18-20 July 2026)
new.eligibility: Degree from a recognised university. Age 21 to 35 years (unreserved and EWS), counted on 1 Aug 2026 per the advert; upper limit 37 for EBC/BC, 38 for women (UR/EBC/BC/EWS), 40 for SC/ST; extra 10 years for PwBD, 5 for ex-servicemen and Jharkhand government servants. Reservation only for permanent residents of Jharkhand. No limit on attempts.
new.application_fee: Rs. 100/- (Rs. 50/- for SC/ST of Jharkhand; no fee for PwBD with 40%+ disability)
new.paper_pattern: Prelims has two compulsory objective papers, General Studies I and II, each with 100 questions of 2 marks (200 marks), 2 hours, set in Hindi and English. Paper II focuses on Jharkhand (history, movement, society, economy, laws). Both papers count for the Mains shortlist (about 15 times vacancies); prelims marks do not count for final merit.
new.selection_process: Prelims (objective) → Mains (6 descriptive papers: qualifying Hindi & English 100 + Language & Literature 150 + 4 GS papers of 200; 950 marks) → Interview (100 marks) → Final merit on 1,050 marks
new.remarks: Mains Paper II requires choosing one of 15 languages, including tribal and regional languages of Jharkhand. Posts change every notification; confirm on jpsc.gov.in.

applicants.note: JPSC notice on CCE 2025 prelims (19 Apr 2026, 564 centres): admit cards issued to 2,17,104 (used as registered); about 1,10,973 appeared in shift 1 and about 1,10,875 in shift 2 (appeared given as the shift-2 figure; JPSC calls both approximate).

vacancies.note: Advt. No. 01/2026 (Jharkhand CCE-2025): 103 posts (Deputy Collector 28, DSP 42, others). Separate backlog adverts 05/2026 and 06/2026 exist and are not counted.

new.notes: All details from official JPSC documents (scanned advert read page by page). Age reckoning date printed as 01.08.2026 in the advert. Prelims result was published 2 Jul 2026 after a High Court order; Mains held 18-20 July 2026. Final result not checked.
